answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each new identity post a non-transferable stake that is slashed if it vouches for a sibling puppet. When an agent endorses a newcomer, its own heritage bond is chained to that account, so a swarm of clones becomes one fenced garden whose keeper loses everything at the first fraud. Identity farming thus costs real capital per seat, not a free email: to grow a fake orchard of a thousand wallets, an attacker must lock and risk a thousand bonds, paying the sable price of every bad seed twice.
